title: The model picks every step, and the loop checks, pauses and stops it
subtitle: Example: "Mark the electricity bill paid and tell me what is still due." The bill id, version and amount are made up; the rules are Billpod's.

steps.label:
a proposal, checked first:
allow-listed, bill exists, version 3

encrypt state into a
10-min resume token

outcome.title: Done in 4 of the 6 model calls, across two HTTP requests
lines: No code wrote "search, then mark paid, then list". Nothing changed until the person said yes.

captions.title: Check the cap, then ask the model
captions.text: Model call 1 of 6. The loop sends the system prompt, the conversation and the tool list. The model cannot run anything: it replies with a tool call, find_bills “electricity”.

captions.title: Run the read at once and send everything back
captions.text: find_bills runs straight away and returns bill b42, version 3 (example). The model remembers nothing, so call 2 resends call 1, its reply and the result. Every call id gets a result.

captions.title: Check the write against stored data before showing it
captions.text: The model asks for `mark_paid` b42, version 3. A tool call is only a proposal: it must be on the allow-list, match its schema, name a bill in this household and carry the version the model read.

captions.title: Save the paused loop and end the request
captions.text: Marking a bill paid needs the person's yes. The loop seals the transcript, the results, the call count and the checked arguments into a 10-minute AES-256-GCM token, shows a card, and the request ends. Nothing is written yet.

captions.title: Resume once and run exactly what was checked
captions.text: Approve sends the token in a second request. The token works once, so a second click gets 409. The loop runs the sealed arguments only, and 2 of the 6 model calls are already used.

captions.title: Stop when a reply has no tool call
captions.text: Call 3 asks for list_due. Call 4 answers in plain text: “Done. Still due: water, 48.20”. That is 4 of 6 calls across two HTTP requests, and no code wrote the order of steps.
